target_customer: Cultivated meat manufacturers needing scale up equipment and services
problem: Cultivated meat production struggles to scale cell growth and scaffolds cost effectively.
business_model: B2B technology and scaling services to cultivated meat makers

founders.name: Anne-Sophie Mertgen
founders.background_notes: Biomedical engineer; later founded Pythag Tech.

competitors.name: Future Meat Technologies
competitors.traction_then: Largest single cultivated meat deal of 2021

competitors.name: UPSIDE Foods
competitors.what: Cultivated meat producer with its own facility
competitors.traction_then: Facility capacity of 50,000 pounds per year

technical_complexity.rationale: Scaling cultivated meat bioprocessing and scaffolds is still unsolved industry wide; a tiny team in Mexico worked from prototypes.

defensibility.rationale: Technology could be defensible if proven, but only prototype stage evidence exists.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action found; sector funding fell sharply after 2021.

market_need_then: Cultivated meat investment topped $1.36B in 2021 and producers needed cheaper scale up, per the Good Food Institute.

branding.community_and_virality: Trade press coverage of Newchip acceptance and a space production partnership with Orbital Assembly in 2022.

brand_strength.rationale: Limited sourced brand presence beyond trade press.

outcome_analysis: Micro Meat was a very early cultivated meat tooling startup in Monterrey that joined YC in Summer 2021 and was accepted to Newchip in August 2022. The cause of its Inactive status is not public. The sector funding drought after 2021 is context only, so macro_downturn is a weak inference and not a sourced cause.
